entry.evidence: few studies have evaluated the effect of tides on river water behavior at the spatial scale of the entire shelf sea

sequences.source_document: Publisher XML full text (jats_text), with the PDF for figure pages

steps.action: Pose the question of how much omitting tides, as climate models commonly do, biases the simulated behaviour of river water on the shelf.
steps.quote: it is necessary to first quantitatively evaluate the impact of tides on the behavior of river water on the shelf

steps.action: Take from estuary-scale studies by other groups the expectation that tides alter river plumes, water age and transport through mixing and residual currents.
steps.quote: [...] suggested that tides can significantly influence shelf hydrodynamics, and thus river water behavior.

steps.action: Narrow the aim to the whole eastern shelf seas of China and three rivers (Yellow, Yalujiang, Changjiang), covering pathways, timescales and concentration.
steps.quote: The present study aimed at a comprehensive understanding of the effects of tides on the river water behavior over the entire shelf

steps.action: Reuse the climatologically forced Princeton Ocean Model of the ESSC with four tidal constituents, set up by co-author Guo and colleagues and validated in earlier studies.
steps.quote: The model for ESSC was initially set up by Guo et al. (2003) and Wang et al. (2008).

steps.action: Drive offline particle-tracking (ECOMSED) and passive-tracer (MERF, TVDal) models and define five diagnostics: emergence probability, transit area, discharge-weighted water age, transit time and tracer concentration.
steps.quote: five indicators (i.e., the emerging probability, transit area, water age, transit time, and tracer concentration) were used to characterize the behavior of the river waters

steps.action: Design paired experiments: a control run with tides and a no-tide case, both analysed with the same diagnostics.
steps.quote: conducted by using the model run with tides (hereafter termed “control run”) and the model run without tides (hereafter termed “no-tide case”)

steps.action: Check that a 3-year hydrodynamic spin-up reaches steady seasonal cycles before the last year is used to drive the offline models (supplement Fig. S1).
steps.quote: run for 3 years which was long enough for the model to get steady seasonal cycles (see Fig. S1 in the Supplement)

steps.action: Compute the control-run pathways of the three rivers from particle emergence probabilities.
steps.quote: most of the Yellow River water passes through the Bohai Strait, enters the Yellow Sea, and finally leaves through the Cheju Strait

steps.action: Compare pathways and transit areas between runs: tides disperse Yellow and Yalujiang water (13 % and 40 %) and concentrate Changjiang water (21 %).
steps.quote: the transit areas of the Yellow and Yalujiang rivers for the no-tide case decreased by 13 % and 40 %, respectively

steps.action: Compute control-run water age, finding multi-year ages in the Bohai and Yellow seas concentrated in the Yellow Sea Cold Water Mass region.
steps.quote: suggesting that the YSCWM region could trap river water and terrigenous materials for several years

steps.action: Compare water age and transit time between runs: removing tides cuts ages by over 80 % in the Bohai and Yellow seas and transit times by 45-93 %.
steps.quote: the tides could significantly slow down the transport of river water over the shelf

steps.action: Derive from the pathway and timescale results the expectation that tides should raise river water concentrations on the shelf.
steps.quote: it is expected that tides would influence the river water concentrations over the shelf

steps.action: Compare tracer concentrations and salinity between runs: no-tide concentrations are about one order lower (73-84 % reductions) and salinity is higher by more than 3 in the estuaries.
steps.quote: the water concentrations of the three rivers in the no-tide case were approximately one order lower in magnitude than those in the control run

steps.action: State a regional pattern across rivers and indicators: tidal effects are stronger in the enclosed Bohai and Yellow seas than in the open East China Sea.
steps.quote: suggesting that the tidal effect on seawater salinity is more significant in relatively enclosed seas than in relatively open seas

steps.action: Pose two rival routes for the tidal effect: tidally changed advection (currents) versus tidally changed mixing.
steps.quote: The river water behavior over the shelf is determined by two processes, namely advection and mixing.

steps.action: Design two hybrid experiments: no-tide runs with control-run diffusivities (tidal-mixing case) or with control-run velocity and sea level (tidal-advection case).
steps.quote: we designed two additional numerical experiments similar to the no-tide case

steps.action: Compare the hybrid cases with the control and no-tide runs: the tidal-advection case reproduces control pathways and long timescales, while the tidal-mixing case resembles the no-tide run.
steps.quote: The river water transport pathways in the tidal–advection and tidal–mixing cases show a similar result to that in the control run and no-tide case, respectively

steps.action: Reject tidal mixing as the dominant route and retain tidally changed currents as the main control on transport rate.
steps.quote: the change in shelf currents induced by tides plays a dominant role in the transport rate of river water over the shelf

steps.action: Compare shelf currents between runs: removing tides strengthens the winter coastal currents and the Yellow Sea Warm Current several-fold.
steps.quote: the coastal currents along the Jiangsu and west Korea in the no-tide case were several times stronger

steps.action: Invoke published mechanisms: tide-wind interaction in quadratic bottom friction, upwind theory for the YSWC, and tidal mixing, residual flow and frontal currents.
steps.quote: which can be explained by the nonlinear interaction between tides and wind-driven current in a quadratic bottom friction term

steps.action: Keep tidally enhanced bottom friction as the dominant mechanism, arguing from the dominance of winter currents in water exchange.
steps.quote: the tidally enhanced bottom friction should be the dominant mechanism

steps.action: Explain the weaker tidal effect in the East China Sea by its open geometry and greater depth.
steps.quote: could be related to both the geometry and the water depth

steps.action: Refine the mechanism river by river and in a schematic: cross-shelf tidal dispersion along Korea for the Yellow and Yalujiang, branch intensification and an eddy for the Changjiang, and dispersion behind the high transit-time SD.
steps.quote: The different tidal effects should be related to the different water transport patterns of the rivers (Fig. 11).

steps.action: Design a parameterized-tide experiment that applies the linear tidal bottom friction of Lee et al. (2000) in the no-tide model.
steps.quote: we added a parameterized–tide experiment (PMT–tide case), wherein linear-type bottom friction considering the tidal effect proposed by Lee et al. (2000) was applied

steps.action: Compare the PMT-tide case with the control run: pathways stay coastal, Yalujiang and Changjiang transit times are off by more than 3.4 years, and estuarine salinity bias exceeds 3.
steps.quote: the tidal parameterization could not significantly improve the simulation of the river water transport pathways and the pattern of the river water age

steps.action: Reject the option that this tidal parameterization can stand in for explicit tides in river water simulation.
steps.quote: the tidal parameterization in a no-tide model could not adequately consider the effect of tides on river water transport

steps.action: Combine the results with published global budgets (runoff, shelf productivity, alkalinity, terrigenous carbon) to argue the consequences for climate and earth system models.
steps.quote: if earth system models or climate models do not explicitly consider tides, the model results will have a large bias

steps.action: Keep the headline claim: tides raise transport timescales 2-10 times and river water concentration by about one order, more so in enclosed seas, so tides should be included in climate models.
steps.quote: the effects of tides on river water behavior should be carefully considered in climate and earth system modeling

tree.answer: Tidal modulation of river water known at estuary scale from earlier studies; effect at the scale of the whole shelf unquantified
No; pathways, ages and river water fractions are diagnosed in a model, not observed
Quantify the tidal effect on pathways, timescales and concentration of three rivers, and its mechanism
Yes, for mechanism: advection vs mixing; bottom friction vs tidal mixing and residual currents; parameterized vs explicit tides
Yes; the tidal-advection and tidal-mixing hybrid runs give distinguishable pathways and timescales
Set in silico: tides switched off, forcing fields swapped, friction parameterized
Weakly: only a spin-up check and a parameterized-tide variant; no observational test, resolution or particle-number sensitivity
Tides slow river water export 2-10 fold through weakened shelf currents; claim kept
Not assessable; the paper was reviewed by Hui Wu and two referees, but no review file was supplied

end.claim: In a regional model of the eastern shelf seas of China, tides lengthen the transport timescales of Yellow, Yalujiang and Changjiang river water by 2-10 times and raise river water concentration by about one order of magnitude, through tidally weakened shelf currents, with stronger effects in the enclosed Bohai and Yellow seas.

decisive_move.sentence: The paired control and no-tide experiments, analysed with identical particle and tracer diagnostics, are the source of every quantified tidal effect; without them no claim exists.

gates.evidence: Action: the stated concern that a no-tide model may bias river water simulation (§1 ¶2) directed the design of the no-tide and hybrid experiments; no data were acquired. Claim: the advection-vs-mixing decomposition (§4.1) and the PMT-tide test (§4.3) could have come out otherwise, but the headline magnitudes were never tested against observations. Registration: nothing is reported as fixed before the runs.

imports.item: Total variation diminishing (TVDal) advection scheme with central-difference diffusion for the offline tracer model

limits: Sub-claims and their status: tidally changed advection (not mixing) dominates the effect, confirmed within the model by the hybrid runs (§4.1 ¶3); tidally enhanced bottom friction as the dominant mechanism, best_explanation argued from cited theory and winter dominance, with no experiment isolating friction from residual currents (§4.2 ¶3); stronger effects in enclosed than open seas, regularity_in_range over three rivers and three seas only (§3.3 ¶2); inadequacy of tidal parameterization shown for a single linear-friction scheme (§4.3 ¶2). Process limits: no comparison with observations is performed here, since model validation is inherited from earlier studies (§2.1 ¶1), so 'estimate_with_resolution' is generous: no uncertainty on the effect magnitudes is given beyond per-day transit-time SDs. No sensitivity tests on grid resolution, particle number, diffusivity, forcing year or emergence-probability grid are reported. Evaporation is ignored in the particle and tracer models (§2.1 ¶1), and re-entry is ignored in age and transit time (§2.4.2 ¶1). Only climatological forcing is used. Inference: swapping velocity or diffusivity fields offline treats advection and mixing as separable, which the paper does not discuss. The spin-up check is coded as a control (comparison against a steady seasonal cycle); that classification is the coder's. Composition is none_fits because the walk is a numerical twin experiment (conditions set computationally, tides on or off) followed by a factorial decomposition of the mechanism, with no observation stage; it resembles strong_inference only in §4.1. The paper makes no explicit 'first' statement, only a gap statement (§1 ¶3). The review statement names an editor and three referees, but no review file was supplied, so changes made in review are unknown. The Figure 14 caption says 'no-tide case' where the PMT-tide case is meant. Code and data are available only on request.

disagreements.support: The paper extends single-aspect, estuary-scale findings to the whole shelf and to several indicators at once.
disagreements.quote: they commonly focused on only one aspect of the river water [...]
